title: Resend MCP Server
summary: Run Resend's official MCP server so your agent can send test emails, manage domains, templates and contacts and check delivery from the chat.
description: Resend's MCP server wraps most of the Resend platform: sending and batching email, templates, contacts and segments, broadcasts, domains, webhooks and logs. It is handy when you build transactional email and want to try a send without leaving the editor.
It runs locally with npx and needs one environment variable, RESEND_API_KEY. You can also set a default sender and restrict which folders it may read attachments from.
useWhen: Send yourself a test of a new welcome email
Check whether a sending domain is verified
List recent emails to see which ones bounced
Draft a template and send it to a staging inbox

mcp.name: resend

env.name: RESEND_API_KEY
env.description: Your Resend API key. A key limited to sending access is enough for test sends.

env.name: SENDER_EMAIL_ADDRESS
env.description: Optional default From address on a verified domain.

env.name: MCP_ALLOWED_FILE_DIRS
env.description: Optional folders the server may read attachments from. Set it to keep file access narrow.

access: Sends real email from your Resend account
Reads and changes domains, templates, contacts and webhooks the key allows

example.prompt: Send a test email from hello@mail.example.com to me@example.com with the subject 'Welcome check' and a one-line body.
example.result: Email queued with id 4f1c...; status delivered after a few seconds. Sent from hello@mail.example.com.

faq.question: Can it email real customers by accident?
faq.answer: It sends to any address you or the agent give it. Use a sending-only key and tell the agent to send to your own inbox while testing.

faq.question: Does it have an HTTP mode?
faq.answer: Yes, resend-mcp can serve Streamable HTTP with the --http flag, where each client sends its own key as a Bearer token. The stdio setup here is simpler for one developer.

access: Sends email and changes settings in the Resend account behind the key
On stdio, file access is unrestricted unless you set allowed folders
